text:
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-api.p99_latency >= 7.5s for 3m, error-rate spike 502s. auto-page -> #incidents :rotating_light:

alice: seeing huge spike in request rate from a few customers, p95 climbing to 1.5s and p99 ~9s. queue length jumped to ~22k. paging oncall.

ben: yep, confirmed in grafana - request.input_queue.len: 22087, inflow QPS 4.1k -> sustained. Hosted GPU pool at 98% util. autoscaler attempted new instances but API rate-limited by cloud provider.

carol: autoscaler logs: 
```
2026-03-15T13:07:21Z ERROR: provisioner: create_instance failed: QuotaExceeded: InsufficientGPUQuota
2026-03-15T13:08:03Z WARN: retrying in 30s (attempt 3/5)
```

ops_oncall: can we temporarily throttle heavy customers? Which routes are hottest?

alice: /v1/generate and /v1/chat both hot. Top 10 tenants making 60% of traffic. Suggest target high-volume keys for soft-rate-limit.

ben: rolling a short config in rate-limiter to apply 50% token throttle for tenant tags [enterprise-batch, ad-crawler-xxx]. command: `kubectl apply -f rate-limit-patch.yaml` (deploy-bot: rolling update triggered).

deploy-bot: roll started for rate-limiter config patch (canary 2 pods -> 10 pods).

carol: autoscaler keep failing because cloud quotas are per-region and our request pattern is across many zones causing quota fragmentation. Opening support ticket with cloud.

ops_oncall: immediate mitigation: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller quantized model variant for best-effort tenants, 2) limit max input length to 512 tokens for non-SLA customers, 3) enqueue very large requests to background job. I'll implement 1+2 now.

ops_oncall: applying routing change -> `curl -X POST https://platform.internal/api/v1/route/override -d '{"match":"tenant:non-sla","model":"gpt-q-8bit","max_input":512}'`

alice: starting support churn analysis. customer-impacted list: 24 tenants with >=1% error-rate increase. prepping incident banner.

support_pg: drafting message: "We're experiencing elevated latency and timeouts for a subset of API requests. We're actively mitigating by throttling high-volume sources and routing to fallback models. We'll update in 30 min."

ben: metrics after throttles + routing: queue length dropped from 22k -> 9k in 12m, p95 -> 800ms, p99 -> 4.6s, error rate trending down but still above baseline. autoscaler still showing provisioning retries.

carol: discovered root cause: cloud quota accounting bug + our provisioner is doing exponential backoff with wide jitter that causes too-sparse retries under sustained high inflow. patch in flight to reduce backoff window and prefer burst retries for short windows.

ops_oncall: patch applied to provisioner (canary). also force-created a small dedicated GPU pool from reserved capacity (dedicated-spot-urgent) to buy headroom: created 6 gpus. manual action succeeded.

ben: after dedicated pool add: GPU utilization (hosted pool) 85% -> 72%, queue length 9k -> 3.2k over next 18m, p99 -> 2.1s, timeouts down 80%.

incident-bot: NOTE: pager handoff scheduled to sre_lead at 14:30 UTC for root-cause follow-up and customer comms.

sre_lead: taking over oncall. ops_oncall do a short write-up of actions and open runbook PR for quota-mitigation play. Also need incident timeline for postmortem.

ops_oncall: write-up: 
- 13:05 UTC: spike detected (Q len ~22k)
- 13:06 UTC: paging triggered
- 13:10 UTC: applied soft-rate-limits to top noisy tenants
- 13:15 UTC: routed non-SLA to quantized fallback + reduced max_input
- 13:22 UTC: discovered cloud quota refusal causing autoscaler failures; reduced backoff and retried
- 13:28 UTC: manually provisioned 6 GPUs from dedicated pool
- 13:40 UTC: queue ~3.2k, p99 2.1s, continuing drain

support_pg: finalized customer banner and posted: "We mitigated the majority of impact; background draining in progress. More details to follow." :thumbsup:

carol: submitted cloud support ticket #CLOUD-9182 and escalation request for temporary quota increase. included log excerpts and autoscaler trace.

ben: note - we saw a secondary small surge at 13:50 probably related to retry storms from SDKs. recommend adding jittered client-backoff guidance to SDK release.

sre_lead: OK — schedule postmortem, assign owners: autoscaler backoff logic -> carol, quota playbooks + reserved pool runbook -> ben, SDK retry guidance -> alice/support_pg. I'll own final RCA and customer-facing timeline.

ops_oncall: leaving detailed metrics + grafana links in the incident ticket. handed to sre_lead. Handoff: all immediate mitigations in place, dedicated pool holding. Please watch for regressions and cloud ticket updates.

sre_lead: acknowledged, taking over. closing pager for ops_oncall.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> services returning to baseline, keep monitoring for 2h.

support_pg: will send a follow-up to affected tenants with a short summary after RCA draft.

alice: final check 14:45 UTC - queue 412, p95 120ms, p99 480ms. Looks stable. Great job team. :party_parrot:

ben: added a temporary monitoring alert: autoscaler.provision_failures.rate > 1/m -> escalate to infra-sig.

carol: PR opened for provisioner backoff fix: https://git.internal/r/redwood/provisioner/pulls/542 (CI queued).

sre_lead: leaving notes for postmortem: mitigation choices, why reserved pool provisioning was necessary, need for automated reserve failover, review of cloud quota tracking.

support_pg: scheduling customer syncs for any tenants with >5% error-blips.

alice: closing thread, will attach logs/timelines to incident ticket 2026-03-15-663001.

incident-bot: thread archived by sre_lead."
